newsitem.title: FRANCE: France tightens tax regime on life assurance.
newsitem.headline: France tightens tax regime on life assurance.

text.p: The French government said on Thursday that it planned to scrap tax breaks on contributions to new life assurance policies, effective immediately.

But it left untouched tax exemptions on proceeds from life assurance policies, although it said these would in future have to pay the CSG income tax, a flat rate of tax being increased to 3.4 percent.

Financial markets had feared a tougher crackdown on life policies, hitting tax exemptions on both contributions and proceeds, which might have hit the bond market. Life assurance companies are major buyers of French government bonds.
In 1995 the government scrapped tax breaks for contributions to life assurance policies for those who paid income tax over 7,000 francs.

The government said that, from September 5, 1996, it was scrapping tax breaks for all new contributions to life assurance policies, apart from contributions due during the life of the policy under a previous agreement.
"Other tax advantages, which life assurance benefits from will remain unchanged. Income from these savings products will nonetheless become subject to the CSG tax," it said.
